module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1014

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1014](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1014)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [OpenAI26] *On the ratio of $R(k,\ell)$ and $R(k,\ell+1)$*, proof due to an internal model at
  OpenAI (2026).
  https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1014

local notation "R(" k ", " l ")" => SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey k l

/--
Let $R(k,l)$ be the Ramsey number, so the minimal $n$ such that every graph on at least $n$
vertices contains either a $K_k$ or an independent set on $l$ vertices.

Prove, for fixed $k\geq 3$, that
$$\lim_{l\to \infty}\frac{R(k,l+1)}{R(k,l)}=1.$$

This has been
[solved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1014.lean"]
theorem erdos_1014 : ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun l : ℕ ↦ (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) / (R(k, l) : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
That proof in fact shows that
$$R(k,l+1)\leq (1+O(l^{-c/k^2}))R(k,l)$$
for some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1014.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ l : ℕ in atTop,
      (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) ≤ (1 + C * (l : ℝ) ^ (-c / (k : ℝ) ^ 2)) * (R(k, l) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1014

reformulations.difference: The quantitative O-bound is expressed as an eventual inequality with an unrestricted real multiplier C, rather than explicitly requiring a positive multiplier.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both the real power of the natural-number base and the Ramsey-number factor are nonnegative. Replacing any witness C by max C 1 therefore increases the right-hand side and gives a strictly positive witness. The converse is immediate. The full quantified equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis (1971), §6, p. 99: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf
On the ratio of R(k,ℓ) and R(k,ℓ+1), Theorem 1, Remark 1, and equation (3): https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf
Cited formal proof, including RamseyProperty, ramseyNumber, and Erdos1014.erdos1014: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1014.lean

Mathlib sources at the reviewed checkout: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/{Basic,Copy,Clique}.lean; Order/Lattice/Nat.lean; Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean; Order/Filter/Defs.lean and AtTopBot/{Defs,Basic}.lean.
review.notes:
Both declarations are faithful. The paper's equation (3), with q=k², supports the absolute exponent constant in the quantitative variant: both terms have power-decay gaps at least 1/2 before logarithmic losses; absorbing those losses and taking q-th roots permits c=1/4, with the coefficient and threshold depending on k.

Lean checks covered R(k,0)=0, R(k,1)=1 for k>0, positivity for positive parameters, and R(3,3)=6. The exceptional l=0 division is harmless for both asymptotic statements. A scratch-only compatibility port of the cited Lean 4.29.1 proof compiled under the sandbox's 4.33.1. Its Ramsey definition was proved equal to classicalRamsey, and the transferred exact main statement depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

The live erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare 403 challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Their current ancillary remarks could not be read; mathematical faithfulness and solved status were checked against the available cited primary papers and formal proof. Detailed evidence is saved in /workspace/review/review_notes.md.
